steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Lightly grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.

Place carrots into a medium pot and cover with salted water; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to medium-low and simmer until carrots are just tender, about 15 minutes. Use a slotted spoon to transfer carrots to a bowl. Add zucchinis to simmering water in the pot and cook until tender, 2 to 3 minutes. Transfer zucchinis to the bowl with carrots. Drain water from the pot, reserving about 1/4 cup cooking liquid.

Add mayonnaise, onion, horseradish, salt, and black pepper to a large bowl. Stir in reserved cooking liquid. Mix carrots and zucchinis into mayonnaise mixture until well combined; pour mixture into the prepared baking dish.
Mix bread crumbs and melted butter in a small bowl until combined; sprinkle over vegetable mixture.
Bake in the preheated oven until bread crumbs are lightly browned, about 15 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Carrot Zucchini Casserole
raw_recipe.description: Tender carrots and zucchini get a little zing from prepared horseradish and mayonnaise in this creamy baked side dish.

review.reviewBody: As a basic recipe it is a good foundation. I cooked the carrots and squash in low-sodium chicken broth (adding 1/2 chopped onion with the zucchini to cook). Increased the horseradish to 1 tsp and added 1/4 tsp garlic powder and 1/4 tsp onion powder for flavor. Made fresh breadcrumbs and added 1 tbsp. Italian blended seasoning to them (again, to heighted the flavor profile). Skipped the grated onion, but added 1/3 c fresh grated parmesan cheese to the topping. You could easily add chopped chicken, browned ground beef of turkey to make it a one dish meal - or keep it as a stellar side dish!

My family actually enjoyed this even though they're usually not the vegetable type. I doubled the recipe, and followed some suggestions from a previous reviewer. I heated the whole carrots an extra 10 minutes so they were soft to cut but not mushy, then added sliced onion with the zucchini, and sprinkled some garlic powder, Italian seasoning, and Badia Sazon Tropical seasoning (orange bottle in Spanish aisle) on the vegetables, and then I added some parmesan cheese and extra Italian seasoning to the Italian breadcrumbs mix. I then heated it for an extra 5 minutes to make it a little toasty.

Chose this recipe because I try to avoid canned soups in recipes and the addition of the horseradish intrigued me. I made three changes. I substituted the grated onion with one diced onion, caramelized in butter. I also instinctively doubled the sauce. Glad I did because it turned out perfectly moist. Third, I mixed in about 1/2 c of a good Parmesan cheese with the bread crumbs and butter for the topping.
This dish is excellent. Quick to make, also makes a nice lunch low in calories. I don't care for horseradish so I substituted about 3T Franks chili sauce. I also used my spiralizer for the zucchini.

Loved this casserole. Made it for dinner guests. They took leftovers home and requested recipe.
Followed recipe ingredients, but used 1 full tsp horseradish.
Easy to make a few days in advance! Bring it to room temp before heating at 350 for 30 minutes.

This is good and easy. I did not pre-cook the zucchini. I microwaved the carrots with 2 slices of onion, then chopped the onion. Added more horseradish as I love how it mellows when baked. Will definitely make again.

I made this recipe with a few changes. I added some cauliflower and ricotta cheese that I had on hand and wanted to use up. This made the perfect filling for vegetable lasagna. I will definitely make this again.

SPOILER ALERT: I MADE CHANGES! Looking to lower my cholesterol through diet, thought I’d give this a try. But cooked carrots make me gag, and they’re high in sugar, so I subbed in a pound of butternut squash. Added garlic powder, onion powder and rosemary to the water. All was going to plan until I realized we were out of horseradish; subbed a heaping teaspoon of minced garlic from a jar. Subbed olive oil for the butter. This actually was surprisingly tasty and I will make it again!
Nice way to eat veggies w/o cheese. I used fat free mayo, panko crumbs and left off butter.. sprayed with Pam to get crunchy..
Didn't have a lot of taste. I spread some 3 pepper cheese on and put it back in the oven and broiled it until the cheese melted. Much better!

I needed a dairy free casserole, and this fit the bill. I cooked the carrots with a little water in the microwave until nearly done, then added the squash (little more water) and all the seasonings and finished them, with the addition of a bit more herbs since one reviewer indicated that it needed something. I then stirred in the mayo and proceeded as directed. My family loved it, but I thought the mayo flavor was a bit overpowering....would like something more savory. I'll make again and play with the flavors. Thanks for a great starter recipe!
We really enjoyed the blend of carrots & zucchini. I made extra liquid (added Greek yogurt instead of more mayonnaise), added rotisserie chicken pieces & served it over rice. Yum!
Sliced carrots and zucchini with mandolin,mixed up everything it turned out very good,even better the next day nice flavor,pleasant change from the cheesy cassarole norm.would make again.

This came out great. I ran the peeled carrots through a food processor with a 4 mm blade. This came out too narrow (4 mm is about 1/8 inch). I cut the zucchini by hand and made 1/4" slices and these came out better. The (thin) carrots cooked faster. I diced a full onion rather than grating one. Otherwise I followed the recipe. I will definitely make this again.

Very tasty. I added 5 chopped mushrooms prezapped in microwave into the sauce mix. Finely chopped the onion rather than grated. Definitely will repeat this. Might add a little garlic next time. Nice savory dish. I thought about adding chopped celery, but didn’t because I felt it would change the overall flavor. Might try that next time, too. Very tasty as is!
Wanted to like it, but all I could taste was the mayonnaise. Seemed unnecessarily greasy.
I didn’t have horseradish so added a teaspoon of Italian seasoning to the vegetable sauce mix. I used almond flour and Parmesan cheese in place of bread crumbs to lower the carbs. My family loved it
Very bland for too much work. Tried to save by adding shredded cheese to no avail.
Very tasty. The slicing takes time, but otherwise it's easy to make.

This was pretty good fresh out of the oven and even better the next day. I used Miracle Whip instead of mayonnaise because that’s what I had on hand. I doubled the horseradish because I love it, and a used a whole small shallot for the grated onion. I really liked the zucchini in this dish but the carrots, not so much. Will probably make again without the carrots.
